newsitem.title: USA: Conoco awarded Trinidad offshore blocks.
newsitem.headline: Conoco awarded Trinidad offshore blocks.

text.p: Conoco Inc said Wednesday the Minister of Energy for Trinidad and Tobago awarded the DuPont Co subsidiary two exploration contracts for offshore blocks east of Trinidad.
The two blocks combined, referred to as 4a and 4b, cover about 300,000 acres and are in water depths ranging from 200 to 2,500 feet.
Conoco said it expects to spend in excess of $50 million to fully evaluate the blocks through seismic and drilling.

The company noted it holds a 41 percent interest in Phoenix Park Gas Processors Ltd, a gas processing plant in Trinidad, as part of a venture with the National Gas Co of Trinidad and Tobago Ltd and Pan West.

In addition to the contracts singed Wednesday, Conoco and other international oil companies are awaiting confirmation of bids placed earlier this year on deepwater blocks in the Atlantic, east of Trinidad.
Conoco said it participated in bids for three of these blocks.

As part of its exploration agreements, Conoco said, it will make an initial contribution of $200,000 to the government of Trinidad and Tobago for technical assistance and equipment. In addition, the company will make annual contributions of $800,000 to the government for administration costs, training of nationals, and research and development efforts. These amounts will increase in the event of a commercial discovery.
Conoco recently made a $50,000 contribution to the University of the West Indies.
